name: rvvm
why: A RISC-V virtual machine that can boot real operating systems, a good way to watch a foreign architecture execute.

brief.what_it_is: RVVM is a virtual machine and emulator for RISC-V guest systems. You give it a RISC-V firmware image (for example OpenSBI plus U-Boot, bundled as fw_payload.bin), optionally a disk image, and memory, core, and display settings on the command line. It then boots the guest OS in a window with a framebuffer display, UART terminal, and keyboard and mouse input. The README also describes a userland emulation mode, still marked WIP, for running RISC-V applications on a foreign-architecture host without a guest OS.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames RVVM as an emulator that emphasizes performance, security, lean code and portability, and says it already runs many guest operating systems, including Linux, Haiku, FreeBSD and OpenBSD. It also aims to run RISC-V applications on a foreign-arch host without full OS guest and isolation.
brief.how_it_works: The README says the CPU runs through a tracing JIT with x86_64, ARM64 and RISC-V backends, and claims this is faster than QEMU TCG. It also lists an interpreter for the RV64IMAFDC instruction set in its contributor notes, and describes a librvvm library API that the rvvm binary builds on. The README does not explain the JIT or the kernel-level isolation mechanism in more detail.

commands_seen.context: Clones the source repository before building with make or CMake.
Builds RVVM with GNU Make, the recommended method in the README.

Example run: two-core VM with 2 GiB RAM and a 1280x720 display, booting OpenSBI and U-Boot firmware with an EFI guest from drive.img, and forwarding host port 2022 to guest SSH port 22.

brief.install_notes: The README gives no brew instructions. Install options listed are: nightly build artifacts via nightly.link, an Arch Linux AUR package named rvvm-git, or building from source with GNU Make (recommended) or CMake, which the README says is extremely portable. Cross-compilation and advanced builds are covered on a wiki page. To actually run a guest you need your own firmware image (OpenSBI and U-Boot in the example) and a guest disk image; the wiki covers recommended firmware and images. Memory defaults to 256M, the machine is 64-bit by default (-rv32 switches to 32-bit), and it is single-core unless -smp is given.
brief.standout: It is a RISC-V emulator with a tracing JIT that the authors claim beats QEMU TCG, and it aims for kernel-level isolation of the guest. It also ships a librvvm library under MPL 2.0 for embedding and for writing new devices, separate from the GPL 3.0 rvvm front end.
brief.status: Looks active but the README gives no release date or commit date. The version badge reads 0.7-git, the build status badge points at the staging branch, and the contributor table and roadmap are current, so the evidence leans toward maintained. I did not check the commit history, so treat this as unknown-leaning-active.
brief.caveats: Userland emulation and shadow pagetable acceleration are both marked WIP. The TODO list includes Svpbmt and Svnapot, a sparse image format, suspend and migration, USB XHCI, sound, a FPU JIT, vector extensions and virtio devices. KVM hypervisor support is an open question in the TODO. VFIO PCIe passthrough needs suitable hardware. The rvvm and rvvm-user binaries are GPL 3.0, while librvvm is MPL 2.0. The RISC-V logo carries a trademark notice and a CC BY-NC font note. The README says it aims for full spec compliance and self-describes it as fully compliant, which is the author's claim rather than something I verified.
quotes: RVVM is a virtual machine / emulator for RISC-V guests, which emphasizes on performance, security, lean code and portability.
